name: Archivio di Stato di Caserta

profile.address: Reggia di Caserta, Piazza Carlo di Borbone, 81100 Caserta, Italy
profile.reading: This is the Archivio di Stato di Caserta, the State Archive of Caserta, in Piazza Carlo di Borbone in Caserta, Italy, operated under Italys Ministry of Culture, formerly named the Ministero dei Beni e delle Attivita Culturali. This registry found no evidence describing the archive as a computing or server data center, and treats its data center style tagging in source data as most likely reflecting its role as a records repository rather than an IT infrastructure facility, recording that distinction honestly rather than fabricating technical specifications. The archive traces its origin to 1812, when it was established as the provincial archive of the historic Terra di Lavoro province, initially based in Capuas Palazzo San Cipriano, later merging with a supplementary archive in Santa Maria Capua Vetere in 1869, operating as a branch of the Naples State Archive from 1927 to 1945 before regaining its own autonomy, and being formally reestablished under its current name in 1963. The archive relocated in 2018 into its current home inside the Reggia di Caserta, the 18th century royal palace built for the Bourbon kings of Naples and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, after previously operating from a roughly 3,250 square meter leased building. Its holdings span roughly 15 kilometers of documents covering the 12th through 20th centuries, including a 1143 parchment sale contract from Aversa believed to be its oldest item, notarial records from the 15th century onward, military district records from 1842 to 1935, police headquarters files from 1880 to 1976, tribunal records from 1808 to 1860, and civil registry records from 1809 to 1865. The Reggia di Casertas broader palace complex includes extensive gardens, a large park, and the historic Aqueduct of Vanvitelli, and its recognition as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997 draws substantial tourism to the city, a context that gives the archives 2018 relocation into the palace added civic and cultural significance beyond simply housing records.
